Q: Why does `-fuse-ld=lld` when targeting `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` cause the binary to dynamically-link the interpreter? A:

Why does this difference exist?

when forcing the lld linker the correct musl dynamic linker /lib/ld-musl-aarch64.so.1 in your case is being used (see official documentation under dynamic linking)

This is because musl provides it's own separate C runtime (separate from lld or gcc's libdl + ld etc.)

You can build musl libc.a without ld-musl-.so (and thus without libc.so) by building a static musl with --disable-shared when configuring.

e.g.,

# Configure, build, and install musl with shared enabled (default) using LLVM tools
./configure --target=${TARGET_TRIPLE} \
      --disable-shared" && \
make -j"$(nproc)" && \
DESTDIR=${SYSROOT:-/} make install

Is it possible to use lld while also getting a fully statically-linked

Technically Yes, but with musl libc.a I'd recommend static archives instead (use $CC -c to compile .o and then put it in a static archive). To build archives from compiled files, e.g. .o) object files you can use ar (e.g., ar rcs out.a in1.o ... in.a ... inLast.o with one or more objects or even other archives)

Hint: you can check with tools like readelf (e.g. readelf -h) or objdump etc. that the builds are indeed static, but I digress
